content.summary_of_the_paper:
This paper investigated the temporal probabilistic model HiT-DVAE combined with attention mechanisms for human motion generation. It
models temporal dependencies between the observations and the latent variables and can be used to generate dynamic poses frame by frame. By evaluating the method on two widely used datasets, HumanEvaI and Human3.6M, the proposed model achieves competitive results compared with other state-of-the-art methods.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
The idea of proposing a deep generative model with sequential latent variables is interesting for me. Compared with generating the whole latent variable, this could be more flexible.
Weakness.
1. I would like to suggest moving the algorithms to the main paper for better clarity. Before reading the supplement, the description in the main paper makes me confused about how to implement during inference. 
2. I would also like to know how the "w" is sampled given x_1:O during testing since during training w ∼ qφw (w|x1:T ).
3. The computational cost & speed of the proposed method compared with the state-of-the-art methods.
4. I would like to see some more visualization videos with dynamic motions given the same input frames.

display_title: Official Review of Paper4469 by Reviewer jxeV

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper introduces a state-space model for the task of 3D human motion prediction. To better handle the inherent stochasticity in human motion, the proposed model incorporates a time-varying latent variable that is updated for every frame, as well as a time-invariant latent variable for capturing sequence-level patterns. The paper leverages graph convolutional networks to process 3D human motion data and multi-head attention to implement the inference and generation networks. The main contribution is the modeling of 3D human motion data with the help of a time-varying latent variable. The contribution is demonstrated on the H3.6M and the HumanEva-I datasets and shows competitive performance in the established benchmarks. The paper also proposes a new set of metrics that focus on the plausibility of the generated samples via an independently trained classifier and overall quality by reporting the performance of the median sample.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths: 

1- The paper is well-motivated. I agree with the potential limitation of the seq2seq-VAE model class. The entire sequence is summarized by a single global latent variable. This can be a problem when the sequences are long and not homogeneous.

2- Moreover, the concerns regarding the established evaluation metrics are valid. Higher diversity may easily result in lower-quality samples. Such samples are not penalized by the metrics reporting error of the best sample.

---

Weaknesses:
Although I agree with the motivation of the paper and think that it could be very useful for the community, I must say that the execution is not good enough.

1- The paper criticizes prior work for using a global latent variable first. Then, in the method section, a global latent variable w is introduced. I could not get the motivation for that. Is it required for a better performance? Moreover, for the inference of this variable, the paper uses a temporal graph convolution network (GCN) with a predetermined number of nodes corresponding to the sequence length. Is it possible to infer the latent variable w from arbitrary length observations? If not, I would consider it a limitation of the proposed model. It removes the variable-length sequence processing ability of the dynamic state-space models.

2- As stated in the contribution statement, this work is not the first Transformer-based model with time-varying latent variables  (see [1*], which is evaluated on the same task).

3- The proposed metrics are not convincing. First, accuracy and the FID score do not correlate. Can it be considered a reliable metric in this case? Second, while I agree with the concerns about reporting the best-performing sample, I am also not convinced by the idea of reporting median errors. It penalizes models that can generate highly diverse and yet plausible samples. If we seek a model where half of its samples resemble the ground truth (this is what the proposed metrics look for), then there is no point in going for the stochasticity.

4- I do not think the ablations are conclusive. On different datasets, different settings achieve the best performance. In fact, the proposed model is not the best setting for the proposed median-based metrics. I am curious how the model would perform in other benchmarks such as the CMU or AMASS.

---

Additional comments:

1- [2*] is a relevant piece of work that should be discussed and included in the baselines.

2- The following statement is not correct: "In previous literature, this is always realized by RNNs (Girin et al., 2021)." Prior work has augmented transformers [1*] and temporal convolutions with dynamic latent variables (see examples in Girin et al.'s work in Sec. 14.2.4).
 
3- The cited work is probably not the correct reference in this statement: “In this paper, we propose a hierarchical DVAE architecture based on the Transformer of Pavlakos et al. (2017).” 

---

Additional References

[1*] Tang, Binh, and David S. Matteson. "Probabilistic transformer for time series analysis." Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 34 (2021): 23592-23608.

[2*] Zhang, Yan, Michael J. Black, and Siyu Tang. "We are more than our joints: Predicting how 3d bodies move." Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition. 2021.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The idea of using time-varying latent variables in 3D human motion modeling is a promising line of research as it has not been extensively studied. The proposed model leverages various building blocks in the dynamic VAE framework and does not introduce any novelties nor include a domain-specific component. This could be tolerated if the paper had proposed a new evaluation procedure or an interesting use case, or presented significantly good results.
content.summary_of_the_review: I am leaning towards rejecting this paper due to the inconsistencies I mentioned in the weaknesses part. The following statement is from the abstract: "The stochasticity in the generative process is thus modeled at the whole sequence level, which is inconsistent with the inherent time-dependent uncertainty of human motion (e.g. people can jump or walk after getting up from a chair)." The paper does not do a good job of demonstrating this problem and its solution. The proposed model is evaluated in the same benchmarks using very short sequences and has not achieved a convincing performance. I do not think that the established benchmarks reveal the merits of the state-space models. See the work of Rempe et al. (2021) showcasing various tasks beyond short-term motion prediction.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper:
The paper proposes a novel method to generate motion sequences. Current motion generation methods attempt to encode an entire sequence of human poses into one latent vector, which is provided to the decoder to generate corresponding motion. The authors claim that time-dependent uncertainty cannot be addressed through such methods, and propose to represent motion as a sequence of latent vectors.

To achieve this, the authors propose to use a dynamical VAE, which is an autoregressive encoder-decoder model. On top of the latent vectors for each time frame, they introduce an additional parameter that captures the context of the entire sequence, which is learnt in an unsupervised manner.

The proposed DVAE model is based on a Transformer architecture. The encoder takes the features of a set of poses and a sampled contextual parameter to produce the distribution parameters corresponding to the latent variable. The decoder takes in the features of the past poses, the contextual parameter, and the latent vectors to produce the ensuing poses and latent vectors.

The authors conduct experiments on 2 benchmark datasets and compare the quality of the generated motion against conventional methods. The results demonstrate that the proposal is able to generate diverse motions without a class specific label.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
## Strengths

### Autoregressive approach to motion generation
The authors propose a novel autoregressive model for modeling human motion. The method tackles the most difficult element of motion, which is the variance introduced by time. The authors propose to separate the time-independent element and the dependent element with different parameters $\mathbf{w}$ and $\mathbf{z}$. The decoder is able to accurately generate future frames by using previous frames and the latent parameters as input.

### Evaluation metrics
The authors point out the issue with the existing metrics that mainly focus on the best generated example. They additionally implement a protocol in which the median sample is used to evaluate the quality and the diversity of the generated motions. They also introduce a classifier to evaluate whether the generated motion accurately resembles the target class, and evaluate how accurate the distribution of the data is. The evaluation in Tables 1 and 2 demonstrate that the proposed method is able to generate motion with high overall quality compared to the existing methods

## Weaknesses

### Evaluation design
The evaluation does not truly reveal the effectiveness of the proposal. The authors propose a generation method that is more aware of the time dependency, enabling generation of motion with varying lengths. However, the experiments do not show the effects of the varying frame lengths. For example, how does the proposed methods and others perform when creating varying number of frames? In the current setting, the authors can easily compare against class-conditioned CVAE methods such as [Petrovich+ICCV2021] and the following work:
> Cervantes, P., Sekikawa, Y., Sato, I., & Shinoda, K. , Implicit neural representations for variable length human motion generation. ECCV 2022

Or, the authors can compare against length-varying method following
> Starke, S., Mason, I., & Komura, T., DeepPhase: periodic autoencoders for learning motion phase manifolds. *ACM Transactions on Graphics (TOG)*, *41*(4), 1-13. 2022

The comparison should focus on either robustness to time dependency or robustness of reconstruction, or both, to truly reveal the strengths of the proposal.

### Validity of the components
The ablation study in Table 3 reveals that there are mixed effects of including and removing certain components of the method. for example, time independent parameter $\mathbf{w}$ seems to have mostly negative effect in terms of generation accuracy, as the model without it performs better in the two datasets. The mixed results cast some doubts to the overall design of the model and the validity of the introduced components. 
Also, the unsupervisedly-learned contextual parameter $\mathbf{w}$  is interesting, but in order to demonstrate its advantage, more classes of motion should be introduced. I believe the advantage of using unsupervised parameter would be the liberation from annotating different motion classes. If there are only few classes, wouldn't the current state of the art class-based generation be enough?
BABEL might be a good candidate for datasets with more classes:
> Punnakkal, A. R., Chandrasekaran, A., Athanasiou, N., Quiros-Ramirez, A., & Black, M. J. BABEL: Bodies, action and behavior with english labels. In Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition pp. 722-731, 2021.

### Similar model in similar tasks
Although the following is based on text, the autoregressive approach seems similar to that by:
> Guo C, Zou S, Zuo X, Wang S, Ji W, Li X, Cheng L. Generating Diverse and Natural 3D Human Motions From Text. InProceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition 2022 (pp. 5152-5161).
As they undertake a more challenging task of generating motion from textual description, some mention to these approaches seem necessary.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
### Clarity and Quality
I believe the paper is clearly written with concise details about the proposal and its components.

### Novelty
I believe the proposal is somewhat novel, although there are already similar research that focuses on autoregressive motion generation given textual description.

### Reproducibility
As details are mostly clear, I believe the reproducibility is high.
content.summary_of_the_review:
In this paper, the authors proposed to tackle the most challenging aspect of motion generation, which is the variation caused by uncertainty along the time axis. The authors proposed a novel two-parameter strategy, where time-dependent and time-independent elements are separately captured to allow generation of ensuing poses based on contextual and temporal information.

I truly appreciate their efforts in proposing a robust model. However, I do not think that the current experimental setting reveals the true values of the proposal. For example, there is no comparison of methods when different number of frames are generated. I believe that the proposal would perform better than the prior methods if it were to produce even longer motion sequences, but such evidence is missing, which is really unfortunate.

Also, the ablation study revealed that the design of time dependent/independent elements may not be optimal, as exclusion and inclusion of various elements seem to have very mixed results without a clear tendency. 

I do understand that this is a difficult problem to tackle, but I believe major revision in the experiments is needed to reveal the values of the proposal.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
